title: T-admissible condensed coefficients and canonical scalar local models
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], with its reconstructed commutative section-ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Put $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$ and let $R\to\Gamma(S,\Lambda)$ be restriction along the terminal map of the profinite set $S$. Define t-admissibility to mean: every finitely generated ideal of $R$ is finitely presented [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]; every finitely presented $R$-module, placed in degree zero in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], is a perfect ring complex [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]; and $R\to\Gamma(S,\Lambda)$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] for every extremally disconnected profinite set $S$. The perfect degree-zero condition expresses a finite resolution by finitely generated projectives.

For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with coefficient ring $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Regard its module sheaves by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], equivalently by the internal-to-sectionwise equivalence already cited. A $\Lambda_X$-module sheaf $M$ has scalar local models if it has a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]: there is a pro-etale covering $\{U_i\to X\}$ and for each $i$ a finitely presented $R$-module $N_i$ with $M|_{U_i}\cong\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes_{\underline R}\underline{N_i}$, where $\underline R$ and $\underline{N_i}$ are constant sheaves and the tensor is taken along the canonical constant-section map $\underline R\to\Lambda_{U_i}$, the inverse image of the counit of the constant-sheaf/terminal-sections adjunction. No common $N_i$ is imposed.

Write $D_\Lambda(X)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of these module sheaves, with ordinary derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_X[0]$. Its dualizable object predicate means admitting a right dual with evaluation and coevaluation satisfying both triangle identities. The predicate that $X$ has Zariski locally finitely many irreducible components means that every point has an open neighbourhood with finitely many irreducible components. For any inherited triangulation on the full dualizable subcategory, define restriction of the standard t-structure to mean the existence of a t-structure whose nonpositive and nonnegative parts in every integer degree are precisely the corresponding ambient standard parts.
